project.objective: Who were the parents of Christiana Clark, born 29 January 1783 in Pennsylvania, who married William Clark, lived in Coshocton County, Ohio, and died 27 December 1848 in Monroe, Green County, Wisconsin?

questions.question: Who were the parents of Christiana Clark, born 29 January 1783 in Pennsylvania and baptized 2 March 1783 at Rehrersburg, Tulpehocken Township, Berks County?
questions.rationale: Christiana Clark has no parents recorded in the tree. Her baptism fact pinpoints Tulpehocken Township, Berks County, Pennsylvania — a heavily German Reformed and Lutheran community with well-preserved church registers running from the mid-1700s. That specificity makes this the highest-value starting point: the registers that recorded her baptism likely recorded her parents as well. Her 1848 death in Green County, Wisconsin and her children's later records (obituaries, death certificates, marriage registers) may also name her parentage. Identifying her parents is the direct and sole objective of this project.

The Ancestry Pennsylvania church marriage search for Adam Schreck (log_063) and the berkshistory.org church record index (log_064) are both handed to the user with no capture returned. Without their results, only one evidentiary unit directly names Christiana Clark's parents: the Altalaha Evangelical Lutheran Church baptism entry, read as the original register image (src_006) and confirmed by the IGI index (src_001) — both deriving from the same 1783 baptism event and the same informant (the presenting parent). The original register image is unambiguous — born 29 January 1783, baptized 2 March 1783 at Rehrersburg, parents Adam Schreck (father) and Margreth (mother) — and no competing baptism was found in any searched collection. The pending searches are most likely to strengthen the conclusion by supplying a marriage record for Adam Schreck and Margreth, not to change it. FamilySearch collections are exhausted for 18th-century Berks County church marriage indexes (pli_004, skip_category: no_coverage).

Berks County tax lists survive from 1752 (loc_001). A Clark family head assessed in Tulpehocken Township across this period would place Christiana's probable father in the community at the time of her birth and through her childhood. Pennsylvania tax assessment lists for this era are typically browse-only image volumes in the FamilySearch catalog — search the catalog for Berks County tax lists and browse the Tulpehocken Township sections ca. 1783-1810. The name Clark (or variant Klar, Klaark, Claar) in an adjacent Berks Township might indicate the family crossed into a neighboring area after the 1810 census gap noted for Tulpehocken.

FamilySearch full-text search covers 348 Berks County probate volumes (Pennsylvania Probate Records, 1683-1994, collection 1999196), which is browse-only (personCount 0) for name search but searchable by full text. A Clark will or administration naming Christiana as a daughter would be direct parentage evidence. Run a full-text co-occurrence search on 'Clark' and 'Christiana' (and variant 'Christina', 'Klar') scoped to the Berks County volumes. Date window to 1850 covers any Clark patriarch who could plausibly have sired a child born in 1783 and outlived her by decades.

items.rationale: FAN item — required for a parentage question. Christiana's children who died in documented jurisdictions after formal death registration began may have informants who knew her birthplace or parents. Priority targets: Mary J Clark (d. 2 Apr 1888, Pike Twp, Coshocton, Ohio), William W Clark (d. 26 Feb 1890, Franklin/Coshocton, Ohio), Elizabeth Clark (d. 12 Mar 1892, Coshocton, Ohio), Samuel Clark (d. 8 Jun 1904, Martin County, Minnesota). Ohio registered deaths from 1867; Minnesota from ca. 1870. Samuel's tree LifeSketch already states 'Irish-German descent,' pointing to Christiana's German Palatine heritage — his death certificate may supply a more specific birthplace or parents. Search FamilySearch Ohio and Minnesota death collections for each child.

Christiana died 27 December 1848 in Monroe, Green County, Wisconsin. Wisconsin's formal death registration did not begin until 1 October 1907, so no death certificate exists. However, Green County probate records (Wisconsin Probate Records on FamilySearch) begin in the late 1840s and may hold an estate file for Christiana Clark naming her next of kin or stating her Pennsylvania origins. An estate deed in the Ohio tree records (79HC-QMK — 'Administrator of C Clark estate to Joseph Clark') shows her Coshocton land was administered after her death; a Green County probate file, if any, would address her Wisconsin assets separately. Date window to 1860 allows for a delayed estate settlement.

The Historical Society of Berks County maintains a free online index of over 1.2 million names from more than 300 local church records at berkshistory.org/library/church-record-index/. This index covers church registers not digitized on FamilySearch and may surface a Clark baptism entry at Altalaha or a neighboring congregation pointing to Christiana's parents. Copies of the underlying volumes can be requested by mail for a fee. Search the online index for Christiana/Christina Clark and variant spellings of Clark in Berks County, then request the relevant volume page if found.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Parents of Christiana Clark (born 1783, Berks County, Pennsylvania)

**Conclusion:** The evidence strongly suggests that Christiana Clark — born 29 January 1783 in Pennsylvania and baptized 2 March 1783 at Rehrersburg, Tulpehocken Township, Berks County — was the daughter of **Adam Schreck** and his wife **Margreth** (maiden name unknown), residents of Tulpehocken Township at the time of her birth.

### Primary Evidence: The 1783 Baptism Record

The sole direct statement of Christiana's parentage is the 1783 baptism entry in the register of Altalaha Evangelical Lutheran Church, Rehrersburg, Berks County, Pennsylvania. The entry appears on the IGI batch extraction sheet (image group 007767897\_013, image 007767897\_00942) as:

> SCHRECK BRN 29 JAN 1783 CHRISTINA D\* ADAM SCHRECK AND MARGRETH 00542-1  
> CHR 2 MAR 1783

This records Christina Schreck as a daughter (D), born 29 January 1783, christened 2 March 1783, parents Adam Schreck and Margreth, at Rehrersburg.[1]

The same event is indexed in "Pennsylvania, Births and Christenings, 1709-1950," *FamilySearch* (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:9MW1-89TP : 16 December 2023), Entry for Christina Schreck, 1783 — a derivative IGI database entry that indexes the same batch extraction sheet.[2]

Both sources transmit the same informant's statement: the presenting parent, a household member with firsthand knowledge of the child's birth date and parentage. They constitute **one evidentiary unit**. The information is **primary** (supplied at the time of the baptism by a household member present) and **direct** (the record expressly names both parents). The source as consulted — the IGI batch extraction sheet — is a derivative of the underlying original handwritten register.

### Identity: Christina Schreck = Christiana Clark

Christiana Clark is identified with the Christina Schreck of the baptism record on four grounds:

1. **Name and maiden name**: The baptism records "SCHRECK / CHRISTINA." Christiana's surname after her marriage to William Clark was Clark; her maiden name was Schreck. The given-name variation between "Christina" and "Christiana" is a routine spelling alternation in German-heritage Pennsylvania and Ohio records of this era.

2. **Birth date and baptism place**: The entry records birth 29 January 1783 at Rehrersburg, Tulpehocken Township, Berks County — matching exactly the birth date and baptism place stated in the project objective.

3. **FamilySearch record attachment**: FamilySearch confirms the IGI record (ark:/61903/1:1:V2NT-CNT) is attached to tree person GP3R-215 (Christiana Clark), establishing an independent corroborative link predating this project's research.

4. **Wisconsin records (1847–1850)**: A Bureau of Land Management tract book entry records "Christiana Clark" as a grantee of Wisconsin land on 28 May 1847 — "United States, Bureau of Land Management Tract Books, 1800-c. 1955," *FamilySearch* (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:62XK-DSYM : Wed Oct 22 13:55:58 UTC 2025), Entry for Christiana Clark, 28 May 1847.[3] A deed dated 1 August 1848 identifies "Christiana Clark of the County of Green and State of Wisconsin" as the purchaser of 40 acres from C. C. Washburne — Wisconsin, Wills and Deeds, 1850-1853 (Green County Register of Deeds), Green County, Wisconsin (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C3Q8-9BHY : accessed 2026-11-04).[4] Green County, Wisconsin probate records from 1850 concern the estate of "Christina Clark" in Monroe — Green County, Wisconsin, Probate Case Files, 1850 (Estate of Christina Clark), Monroe, Green County, Wisconsin (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:939J-HBPZ-7 : accessed 2026-11-04).[5] Christiana Clark died 27 December 1848 in Monroe, Green County, Wisconsin; these records anchor the same woman in Wisconsin by name and place in the years immediately surrounding her death.

No competing baptism entry was found for any person named Christina or Christiana Schreck, or any other candidate matching the name and date, in the searched collections.

### Corroborating Evidence

A Crawford County, Ohio genealogical directory (compiled church and deed abstracts), 1995 (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QHN-B3BS-8GVR : accessed 2026-11-04)[6] cites a Tulpehocken baptism entry — dated 27 August 1795 — placing "Adam Schreck" as a father of a child at Tulpehocken. This authored, compiled secondary source independently places Adam Schreck in Tulpehocken Township during the period consistent with the 1783 baptism. It is classified as indeterminate quality (an authored compilation drawing from church abstracts of uncertain transcription accuracy) and is treated as corroborating rather than independent direct evidence.

Samuel Clark, a son of Christiana Clark, died in Martin County, Minnesota on 8 June 1904. His death was registered in two derivative Minnesota indexes: "Minnesota, Death Records and Certificates, 1900-1955," *FamilySearch* (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FDMK-8V5 : Fri Mar 27 23:12:33 UTC 2026), Entry for Samuel Clark and \<Unknown\>, 8 June 1904[7]; and "Minnesota, Deaths, 1887-2001," *FamilySearch* (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:HRZB-XVN2 : Fri Mar 27 23:12:33 UTC 2026), Entry for Samuel Clark, 8 Jun 1904.[8] Both records note his father's birthplace as "Germany," consistent with Adam Schreck's German Palatine heritage — Schreck is a German surname and the Tulpehocken Valley was settled predominantly by German Palatine immigrants. These are derivative records with secondary informants (family members not present at Samuel's birth ca. 1820), so the corroboration is weak but consistent with the concluded parentage.

### Conflict Noted and Resolved (c\_001)

A conflict arose between the two 1904 Minnesota death-record indexes: one records Samuel Clark's birthplace as "Ireland" (src_004) and the other as "Ohio" (src_005), both indexing the same underlying death registration. This conflict (c\_001) was resolved by research: "Ohio" is consistent with the documented Clark family residence in Coshocton County, Ohio through the 1820s, while "Ireland" appears to reflect a conflation of the family's German-Irish ethnic self-identification with the actual Ohio birthplace, reported by a secondary informant approximately 84 years after the event. This conflict does not bear on Christiana Clark's parentage.

### Outstanding Searches

Two searches were placed in the researcher's hands without results returned: (1) an Ancestry search of Pennsylvania church marriage records for a marriage of Adam Schreck and Margreth in Berks County, Pennsylvania, ca. 1760–1800; and (2) a search of the Historical Society of Berks County church record index at berkshistory.org. Both were designed to surface a second independent direct statement of the parental couple and potentially establish Margreth's maiden name. A prior search of 18th-century Berks County church marriage registers on FamilySearch — 14 searches across five collections with four spelling variants of Schreck — confirmed those collections do not index Berks County Reformed/Lutheran marriages from 1760–1800. FamilySearch collections for 18th-century Berks County church baptisms (Altalaha and Host Reformed) were fully searched; no competing baptism entry for a Schreck child matching Christina's date was found.

Margreth's maiden name has not been established by the evidence gathered so far; the pending Ancestry and berkshistory.org searches remain the most likely paths to that information.

### Conclusion and Tier

The evidence strongly suggests that **Christiana Clark was the daughter of Adam Schreck and Margreth (maiden name unknown)** of Tulpehocken Township, Berks County, Pennsylvania. The tier is **probable** because: (1) direct parentage evidence rests on a single evidentiary unit — one 1783 baptism event transmitted in two derivative forms, not two independent original sources; (2) two reachable searches remain outstanding and have not yet returned results; and (3) the mother's maiden name has not been established. A marriage record for Adam Schreck and Margreth in Berks County, Pennsylvania, ca. 1760–1800 would be the most significant corroborating evidence and could also supply Margreth's maiden name. Research-plan can stage that search if the researcher wishes to pursue a higher tier.

# Locality Guide: Berks County, Pennsylvania (ca. 1750–1850)
## Focus: Parentage of Christiana Clark, baptized 2 March 1783 at Rehrersburg, Tulpehocken Township

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** 11 March 1752 from Chester, Lancaster, and Philadelphia Counties
- **County seat / administrative center:** Reading
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Pennsylvania
- **Population during period:** 1790: 30,189; 1800: 32,407; 1810: 43,146; 1820: 46,275; 1830: 53,152; 1840: 64,569; 1850: 77,129 (source: Berks County, Pennsylvania Genealogy, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Berks_County,_Pennsylvania_Genealogy)
- **Economy:** Mixed farming, iron forges and furnaces, local mills; Tulpehocken Township was agricultural German Palatine settlement
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly German Palatine immigrants and their descendants in Tulpehocken; some Welsh, Scots-Irish, and English elsewhere in the county
- **Religious denominations:** German Lutheran and German Reformed (dominant in Tulpehocken); Quaker (Oley, Exeter, Maiden Creek, Robeson areas); Mennonite; Moravian; smaller Episcopal, Presbyterian, and Methodist presence
- **Key historical events:** French and Indian War (1750s, frontier impact); Revolutionary War (1775-1783, militia records, loyalist tensions); War of 1812; county growth through the early republic

## Boundary changes
- Formed 11 March 1752; boundaries were largely stable through 1850, though interior township lines shifted
- Records before 1752 for what became Berks County are mostly in Philadelphia, Lancaster, and Chester County records
- Lebanon County was carved from Dauphin County in 1813; for northwestern Berks-area families with any connection to that region, check Dauphin County records before 1813 and Lebanon County after
- No courthouse fires or known record losses in Berks County (Berks County, Pennsylvania Genealogy)

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start dates (county level):** Births and deaths: 1852-54 (low compliance), 1893 (improved compliance). Marriages: 1852-54, then 1885 (high compliance from 1885). Statewide registration of births and deaths began January 1906, with general compliance by 1915. (Pennsylvania Vital Records, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pennsylvania_Vital_Records)
- **What exists for 1750-1850:** No civil vital records exist for this entire period. Church registers are the only vital records.
- **Where held:** Berks County Courthouse (Register of Wills/Orphans Court), 633 Court Street, Reading, PA 19601 — holds birth and death records 1894-1905, marriage records from 1885, probate from 1752. Pennsylvania State Archives (Harrisburg) holds birth/death certificates 1906-1974.
- **Gaps:** Complete gap for 1750-1850; the 1852-54 county registration had very low compliance.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church baptismal, marriage, and burial registers are the essential substitutes for all vital events in this period.

### Church records (PRIMARY SOURCE for this research question)
- **Denominations present in Tulpehocken Township:** German Lutheran (dominant) and German Reformed (closely allied, often sharing buildings); smaller Mennonite, Moravian
- **Union church practice:** Lutheran and Reformed congregations throughout Berks County routinely shared buildings, alternating services. A family record may appear in either or both registers. Always search both.
- **Record types:** Baptisms (naming parents and sponsors), confirmations, marriages, burials, communicant lists
- **Directly relevant congregations and their FamilySearch resources:**
  - **Altalaha Evangelical Lutheran Church, Rehrersburg** (the congregation that recorded Christiana Clark's baptism): Register 1757-1842, imageGroupNumber 007767897_013, 150 images — **browse-only** (0% indexed, not full-text searchable); must be examined image by image. IGI Batch C511431 indexes baptisms 1757-1842 and is searchable at FamilySearch records search — search this first.
  - **Host Reformed Church, Tulpehocken Township** (the Lutheran congregation's Reformed partner): Register 1738-1828, browse-only fragments at FamilySearch (imageGroupNumbers 124102177_002, 124102177_003, 124102177_004). IGI Batch C504581 (baptisms 1740-1875) and Batch M504581 (marriages 1740-1875) are searchable at FamilySearch.
  - **Little Tulpehocken / Christ's Church Evangelical Lutheran, Jefferson Township** (adjacent): IGI Batch C507541 (baptisms 1726-1846), Batch M507541 (marriages 1735-1750).
- **Broader indexes:** The Historical Society of Berks County online index (berkshistory.org/library/church-record-index/) covers over 1.2 million names from 300+ Berks County churches and is free to search — it points to volumes held at the society. Copies available by mail for a fee. The Berks County Genealogical Society (berksgenes.org) also holds church record transcriptions viewable in person.
- **Statewide compilations:** John T. Humphrey, *Pennsylvania Births, Berks County 1710-1800* (2 vols., 1997-98) — FS Library Book 974.816 K2h — transcribes baptismal records from multiple Berks County churches and is a key finding tool. Pennsylvania, Church and Town Records 1708-1985 (Ancestry subscription, collection 2451). Pennsylvania, Historical Society of Pennsylvania, Births and Baptisms 1520-1999 (FamilySearch, collection 4138679, indexed + images).
- **Language:** Registers in this period are mostly in German, occasionally in Latin. Reading skills in German script (Kurrentschrift) are required for the original volumes.
- **Where held:** Originals largely at the Historical Society of Berks County (Reading) or with individual congregations; FamilySearch holds microfilmed/digitized copies of many.

### Census records
- **Federal census:** 1790, 1800, 1810, 1820, 1830, 1840, 1850 — all available for Berks County. Heads of household only until 1850 (all household members named from 1850 onward).
- **Critical gap:** The 1810 census images for Berks County at FamilySearch and Ancestry are missing Tulpehocken Township. Some Tulpehocken residents appear in the Bern Township section. (Berks County, Pennsylvania Genealogy)
- **1820 census:** Digitized at FamilySearch, imageGroupNumber 004433232_001, browse-only (0% indexed). Also available indexed on Ancestry.
- **1840 census:** Digitized at FamilySearch, imageGroupNumber 004410637_002, browse-only (0% indexed).
- **Tax lists as census substitutes (see Tax Records section):** 1752, 1767, 1784, 1798 tax lists name heads of household and are essential substitutes for the gap years.
- **Access:** Federal censuses are indexed on FamilySearch (free) and Ancestry (subscription). Pennsylvania Mortality Schedules 1850-1880 (FamilySearch collection 3512181) may name persons who died within the year preceding each census.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, intestate administrations, guardianship bonds, inventories, accounts, Orphans Court minutes
- **Date range:** Berks County probate records begin 1752 (Berks County, Pennsylvania Genealogy)
- **Testate vs. intestate:** Search both the will book and the administration book. Parents who died intestate will appear in administration bonds naming the widow and sometimes the heirs; guardianship bonds name minor children and therefore can establish both the child's parentage and the guardian.
- **Online access:**
  - Pennsylvania Probate Records 1683-1994 (FamilySearch collection 1999196) — images only, 3.2 million images. Browse-only but full-text searchable via FamilySearch full-text search tool.
  - Pennsylvania Wills and Probate Records 1683-1993 (Ancestry collection 8802) — indexed + images (subscription).
  - Berks County estate files 1752-1799 (FamilySearch imageGroupNumber 005538055_001) — 1816 images, full-text searchable, 0% name-indexed. Additional single-estate volumes at imageGroupNumbers 005538055_002, _003, _004.
  - Register's Docket 1832-1870 (FamilySearch imageGroupNumber 005537934_004) — 90 images, full-text searchable.
  - Orphans' Court Minutes and Probate Records 1751-1792 (FamilySearch Catalog no. 271340) — indexed + images.
  - Register's Docket 1832-1911 (FamilySearch Catalog no. 498886) — indexed + images.
  - *Abstract of Wills of Berks County, Pennsylvania* (abstracts by Jacob Martin and John P. Smith) — available online via FamilySearch Digital Library (catalog no. 272830); also *Abstracts of Berks County Wills 1752-1785* by F. Edward Wright (FamilySearch Library).
- **Where held:** Berks County Courthouse, Register of Wills, 633 Court Street, Reading, PA 19601.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds (Pennsylvania was not surveyed by the rectangular system). Land was granted through warrants issued by the Pennsylvania Land Office in Philadelphia.
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** The Pennsylvania Land Office (Philadelphia/Harrisburg) issued warrants and patents. The Recorder of Deeds in Reading holds county deed books from 1752.
- **Types:** Warrants, surveys, patents, deeds, mortgage records, sheriff sale deeds, land grants
- **Date range:** Berks County land records begin 1752. Earlier warrants for the Tulpehocken Valley are in Philadelphia County or the Pennsylvania State Archives.
- **Online access:**
  - Berks County Deeds 1734-1866 and indexes 1752-1926 (FamilySearch Catalog film 20739, first of 76 films) — images only, browseable.
  - Warrant Register 1682-1950 (FamilySearch imageGroupNumber 008248357_003) — 94 images, full-text searchable.
  - Miscellaneous deeds 1755-1784 (FamilySearch imageGroupNumber 005537934_002) — 39 images, full-text searchable.
  - Pennsylvania Land Warrants and Applications 1733-1952 (Ancestry collection 2350) — indexed + images (subscription).
  - Pennsylvania Tax and Exoneration 1768-1801 (Ancestry collection 2497) — indexed + images (subscription).
  - 1752 List of Taxables, Berks County (FamilySearch Digital Library, catalog no. 246194) — available free online.
  - 1767 Berks County, Pennsylvania Archives / tax index (FamilySearch Library, catalog no. 468121).
  - Pennsylvania US Direct Tax Lists, 1798 (Ancestry collection 2060) — indexed + images (subscription); names property owners.
  - Pennsylvania Land Warrants 1733-1987 (Ancestry collection 2409).
  - Mortgage Records 1752-1822 (FamilySearch films 929921-929935); Miscellaneous Records 1752-1869 (films 929936-929962).
- **Where held:** Berks County Recorder of Deeds, 633 Court Street, Reading, PA 19601. Pennsylvania State Archives (Harrisburg) holds the original warrants and surveys.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts in period:** French and Indian War (1754-1763), Revolutionary War (1775-1783, the most likely to name parents of an 1783 child), War of 1812
- **Record types:** Militia muster rolls, pension applications, bounty land warrants, Revolutionary War pension files (which frequently name wife and children in affidavits)
- **Online access:**
  - Pennsylvania Revolutionary War Battalions and Militia Index 1775-1783 (Ancestry collection 2591)
  - Pennsylvania War of the Revolution: battalions and line 1775-1783 (Ancestry collection 26217)
  - U.S. Revolutionary War Pension and Bounty-Land Warrant Applications 1800-1900 (Ancestry collection 1995) — pension narratives often name wives and children with dates and places
  - Revolutionary War soldiers' pension applications for Berks County 1785-1786 (FamilySearch imageGroupNumber 005537934_001) — 71 images, 1% indexed
  - Pennsylvania Veterans Card Files 1775-1916 (Ancestry collection 62200)
- **Where held:** National Archives (NARA), Washington D.C., and Pennsylvania State Archives

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** Church cemeteries at Altalaha Lutheran (Rehrersburg), Host Reformed Church, and surrounding township churches. Altalaha Lutheran Church cemetery inscriptions 1850-1910 (FamilySearch imageGroupNumber 124254538_001, browse-only) and burial records 1840-1963 (imageGroupNumber 008192927_001, 83% indexed + images).
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave (findagrave.com), BillionGraves, PAGravestones (pennsylvaniagravestones.org), PAGenWeb Archives (usgwarchives.net/pa/berks/cemet.htm)
- **Tombstone transcription collections:** The Schuyler C. Brossman Collection of Cemetery Inscriptions from various Berks County cemeteries (FamilySearch imageGroupNumber 007856346_016) covers Tulpehocken Township 1794-1963; browse-only.
- **Physical records:** Pennsylvania Cemetery Records ca. 1700-ca. 1950 (FamilySearch collection 3743478) — indexed + images

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** The Reading area had German-language and English-language newspapers from the late 18th century. *Der Readinger Adler* (German) began in the 1790s. These may contain marriage notices, administrator notices, and sheriff sale notices naming property owners.
- **Where held:** Chronicling America (LOC) has some Pennsylvania newspapers digitized. GenealogyBank covers 1719-1995. Pennsylvania Newspapers 1795-2009 (MyHeritage, subscription). Pennsylvania, U.S., Newspapers.com Stories and Events Index 1800-current (Ancestry).
- **Content value:** Sheriff sale notices and estate administrator notices in newspapers routinely name heirs and can establish family relationships.

### Immigration and emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** Philadelphia (primary port for German Palatine immigration, 1727-1776)
- **Record types:** Philadelphia ship passenger lists 1727-1808 (German immigrants were required to sign oaths of allegiance; the printed lists name the ship, date, and passengers); naturalization records
- **Online access:**
  - Index to 30,000 Immigrants — German, Swiss, Dutch and French — into Pennsylvania 1727-1776 (Ancestry collection 10413; also at FamilySearch as ebook)
  - Names of Foreigners Who Took the Oath of Allegiance 1727-1775 (Ancestry collection 48365)
  - Pennsylvania Naturalizations 1740-1773 (Ancestry collection 4259)
  - Berks County Naturalization Records 1798-1832 (FamilySearch imageGroupNumbers 007787931_001 and 007787931_002) — full-text searchable, 0% name-indexed
  - Prothonotary's Office naturalization records from 1795 (Berks County Courthouse)
- **Content note:** German Palatine immigrants in the Tulpehocken Valley arrived primarily 1717-1750. The parents of an 1783-born child would likely be American-born; check the grandparent generation in the ship lists.

### Tax records
- **Types:** County tax lists (taxables), proprietary tax lists, US Direct Tax 1798
- **Date range:** Extant from 1752 for Berks County
- **Online access:**
  - 1752 List of Taxables, Berks County (free online: FamilySearch Digital Library, catalog no. 246194)
  - 1767 Berks County, Pennsylvania Archives — tax index (FamilySearch Library, catalog no. 468121)
  - 1767 Tax List (Proprietary), Berks County (FamilySearch Library, catalog no. 478829)
  - 1784 Berks County; Pennsylvania Archives (FamilySearch Library, catalog no. 781289)
  - Pennsylvania Tax and Exoneration 1768-1801 (Ancestry collection 2497) — indexed + images
  - Pennsylvania US Direct Tax Lists 1798 (Ancestry collection 2060) — indexed + images
  - Pennsylvania Published Archives Series 1664-1902 (Ancestry collection 2206) includes Berks County tax lists from the Pennsylvania Archives series
- **Substitute value:** Annual tax lists name heads of household and can substitute for missing census years, track property acquisition, and confirm presence in a specific township.

### Other record types
- **Bible records:** Berks County Bible records are held at FamilySearch (catalog nos. 479260, 479447, 479743, 98517 — the last specifically covering Tulpehocken Township families Brossman, Deck, Weidman). USGenWeb Archives also has transcribed Berks County Bible records.
- **County and local histories:** *1723-1973: Two Hundred Fifty Years Tulpehocken* (FamilySearch Digital Library, catalog no. 240410, available free online) — a collected history of the Tulpehocken area that may name early families. County court records 1755-1782 (FamilySearch Digital Library, 3 vols., catalog no. linked from the genealogy wiki page) name parties in suits and may reveal family relationships.
- **Occupation/biographical records:** Biographies and occupation records for Berks County 1749-1974 (FamilySearch imageGroupNumbers 007951160_001 and 007951160_002) — full-text searchable.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Pennsylvania Births and Christenings 1709-1950 (7.5M persons indexed); Pennsylvania Probate Records 1683-1994 (3.2M images, full-text searchable); Pennsylvania County Marriages 1775-1991 (3.6M records); Berks County estate files 1752-1799 (full-text searchable); Berks County church registers (browse-only images, 817 total volumes) | Free |
| Ancestry | Pennsylvania Wills and Probate Records 1683-1993; Pennsylvania Tax and Exoneration 1768-1801; Pennsylvania Church and Town Records 1708-1985; Pennsylvania Land Warrants 1733-1952; Index to 30,000 German/Swiss Immigrants 1727-1776; Pennsylvania Revolutionary War records | Subscription |
| Historical Society of Berks County | Church record name index (1.2M+ names, 300+ churches) at berkshistory.org/library/church-record-index/ | Free index; fee for copies |
| FamilySearch Digital Library | *1723-1973: Two Hundred Fifty Years Tulpehocken* (catalog 240410); 1752 List of Taxables (catalog 246194); Abstract of Wills (catalog 272830) | Free |

**Coverage of this survey:** The volume_search returned 817 total digitized volumes matching Berks County for 1750-1850 (complete result set). The 50 volumes detailed above represent the first page only; 767 additional volumes were not individually examined. Among the 817 volumes: 242 Religious volumes (219 browse-only), 163 Baptism (156 browse-only), 348 Probate (1 browse-only, 327 full-text), 109 Land (96 full-text).

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Berks County Courthouse, Reading PA 19601 | Probate from 1752; land/deed records from 1752; court records from 1754; naturalization from 1795; marriage records from 1885; birth/death 1894-1905 | In-person or mail request |
| Historical Society of Berks County, Reading | Church records (originals or copies for 300+ churches), Bible records, cemetery transcriptions, county histories | In-person; mail request with fee |
| Berks County Genealogical Society | Church record transcriptions, local genealogies | In-person |
| Pennsylvania State Archives, Harrisburg | Land warrants and surveys; original birth/death certificates 1906-1974; colonial and revolutionary records | In-person or online request |
| National Archives (NARA), Philadelphia | Federal census originals; naturalization records (federal courts); some pension files | In-person |

## Records NOT online
- Original Altalaha Lutheran Church register 1757-1842 (the congregation that baptized Christiana Clark): images are on FamilySearch (browse-only) but the full original register is at the Historical Society of Berks County or with the congregation
- Host Reformed Church register (1738-1828): partial browse-only images at FamilySearch; the full original is at the Historical Society of Berks County
- Berks County annual township tax lists (most years other than those digitized above)
- Berks County Orphans Court minute books and guardianship bonds in full
- Local church records for many smaller Tulpehocken-area congregations: not digitized, only indexed in the Historical Society's online index

## Known record losses
No tool result returned for this survey documents any courthouse fire or record destruction in Berks County. The FamilySearch Wiki page for Berks County (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Berks_County,_Pennsylvania_Genealogy) states: "There is no known history of courthouse disasters in this county." The Pennsylvania Vital Records page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pennsylvania_Vital_Records) lists Erie, Franklin, and Mercer Counties as having losses — Berks County is not among them.

## Research tips
- **Search the IGI batch for Altalaha Lutheran Church first.** The IGI Batch C511431 (Altalaha Evangelical Lutheran Church, Rehrersburg, Baptisms 1757-1842) is searchable at FamilySearch records search and may surface Christiana Clark's 1783 baptism entry with her parents named directly. If the entry appears, note the parents' names and then browse the original images (imageGroupNumber 007767897_013) to verify and find sibling entries. (Source: Berks County, Pennsylvania Church Records, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Berks_County,_Pennsylvania_Church_Records)
- **Search both the Lutheran and Reformed registers.** Because Lutheran and Reformed congregations shared Union church buildings in Tulpehocken Township, a family might appear in either register or both. After searching Altalaha Lutheran (Batch C511431), search Host Reformed Church (Batch C504581 for baptisms; Batch M504581 for marriages). (Source: Berks County, Pennsylvania Church Records)
- **Use the Historical Society of Berks County church index.** The free online index at berkshistory.org covers over 1.2 million names from 300+ churches. Search the surname(s) of suspected parents in this index to find records not available in any digitized form. (Source: Berks County, Pennsylvania Church Records)
- **Check the Humphrey compilation.** John T. Humphrey's *Pennsylvania Births, Berks County 1710-1800* (FS Library Book 974.816 K2h) transcribes baptismal entries from multiple Berks County churches for the 1710-1800 period and includes a list of churches drawn upon. This is a critical finding tool that cross-indexes surnames across congregations. (Source: Berks County, Pennsylvania Church Records)
- **Work the probate records for the parents' generation.** A father or mother of Christiana (born 1783) would likely have died between ca. 1800 and ca. 1840. Wills and estate administrations from that window, searchable via Pennsylvania Wills and Probate Records 1683-1993 (Ancestry) and the FamilySearch full-text search of Pennsylvania Probate Records 1683-1994, may name her directly as a daughter and heir. The *Abstracts of Berks County Wills 1752-1785* (catalog no. 2736310) is a useful printed shortcut for the earliest period.
- **Tax lists are essential substitutes for missing census years.** The 1752, 1767, 1784, and 1798 tax lists name heads of household by township. Finding a suspected father's name in Tulpehocken Township across multiple list years establishes presence and can be combined with church entries to build a family cluster. The 1752 list is free online at FamilySearch Digital Library.
- **Note the 1810 census gap.** Tulpehocken Township is missing from the 1810 federal census images. If a suspected family disappears in 1810, search the Bern Township section of the same census volume and also rely on the 1807-1810 tax lists or church records as substitutes. (Source: Berks County, Pennsylvania Genealogy)
- **Apply German naming patterns.** In Pennsylvania German families, the first daughter was commonly named for the maternal grandmother and the second for the paternal grandmother. The name 'Christiana' in an 1783 baptism likely reflects a grandmother's name (maternal or paternal) that will appear in an earlier church entry — look for 'Christina' or 'Christiana' in the communicant lists or in an earlier generation's baptismal entries in the same congregation.
